clips.text_zh: 又見DOGE post 🙄 DOGE 3日內上太空喎，你又唔買。爆咗都會升啦，唔係就SNL 2.0結局。細注試下又點啫。我今個月CFD已經輸到入肉，DOGE都唔敢再溝⋯當睇戲啦
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to fucking space in 3 days and you're not buying. If this thing explodes it will still move up, so why not ape a bit, then sell before it becomes SNL 2.0? Or maybe it will just start the hype again. Posted on /biz/ today.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread hyping a DOGE catalyst in 3 days

signal.rationale: OP implies a small long position before the catalyst, with intent to sell into the pump

clips.text_en_b2: Doge is genuinely heading to space within three days, yet you're still sitting on the fence. Even if this thing turns out to be a non-event, momentum alone could carry it higher before everything unravels. Picture SNL 2.0 if it flops, or the hype simply reignites. Some anons are throwing in a small position just to ride the wave. I dropped my CFD margin hard this month, so I'm merely spectating. Posted on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_c1: Doge is, quite frankly, hurtling toward the stratosphere within seventy-two hours, and yet you remain stubbornly on the sidelines. If the announcement detonates the way insiders expect, the price will almost certainly rip upward regardless of underlying fundamentals; the prudent play is therefore to allocate a modest position and offload before sentiment deteriorates into an SNL-style rout. Conversely, should momentum reignite the broader rally, latecomers will be left chasing. One cannot help but notice the thread appeared on /biz/ today, which in itself is worth reading carefully.
clips.text_en_c2: Doge is purportedly en route to the stratosphere within the next seventy-two hours, yet one persists in abstaining — a posture that strikes me as almost perverse given the prevailing asymmetry. Should the anticipated catalyst materialise, even a fleeting repricing would more than compensate for a measured position; should it spectacularly implode, one merely averts the SNL 2.0 dénouement that still haunts retail lore. What, then, is the objection to a token allocation, however modest? I, for my part, have been so comprehensively eviscerated by CFD exposure this month that even Doge feels untouchable — my brokerage account reduced, in effect, to a cadaver. Consider it theatre, then: popcorn, detachment, and the quiet consolation that schadenfreude, if nothing else, remains reliably on offer.

clips.text_zh: 今日睇Tesla同SpaceX兩邊都熱，Musk一出X post成個板都震下。我啲prop firm倉太集中喺TSLA，遲啲要分散啲。今晚谷FE chapter 3先 🤮
clips.text_en_b1: Musk stuff is everywhere tonight — TSLA earnings buzz, SpaceX Starship test updates, Optimus progress clips on X. When Musk posts, the whole sector moves. Some /biz/ anons are rotating into TSLA calls while waiting on the next Starship launch date. Crazy how one account can shake the market like that.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread linking Musk policy moves to market action

signal.rationale: OP frames Musk as a market-moving force; TSLA calls implied as the cleanest expression

clips.text_en_b2: Musk-related content is dominating every feed tonight, with TSLA earnings chatter heating up alongside fresh SpaceX Starship test footage and the usual Optimus progress clips circulating on X. The moment he posts anything, the entire sector reacts almost instantly. A handful of /biz/ anons are rotating capital into TSLA call options while they wait for the next confirmed Starship launch window. It is frankly remarkable how a single account can rattle the market like this.
clips.text_en_c1: Tonight the Musk ecosystem is exhibiting an unusual degree of coordinated activity: TSLA earnings speculation is intensifying, fresh Starship test footage is fuelling discussion, and Optimus development clips are once more dominating timelines. Whenever that single account publishes, the entire sector seems to pivot in response, which is frankly staggering when one stops to consider it. On /biz/ certain anons are quietly rotating capital into TSLA call options while they wait for the next Starship launch window to be confirmed. My proprietary-firm book, regrettably, remains disproportionately exposed to Tesla, and I have resolved to diversify the allocation before further concentration risk erodes the account.
clips.text_en_c2: Musk-related stimuli are saturating the discourse tonight — TSLA earnings chatter reverberates alongside SpaceX Starship telemetry leaks, while Optimus demonstration footage circulates on X with metronomic regularity. The phenomenon is, on reflection, almost liturgical in its predictability: a single keystroke from one account, and the entire risk-on complex shudders accordingly. Several /biz/ regulars are, accordingly, rotating capital into near-dated TSLA calls rather than awaiting the next confirmed Starship window, a posture predicated on contango and volatility alike. That one individual can summon such dislocation — that a personal feed can function, in effect, as a sovereign macro signal — remains, to my mind, the most disquieting feature of this peculiar cycle.

clips.text_zh: 今日返工地做斜坡survey，搵到一處factor of safety得1.05⋯真係揸頸。要design soil nail加返上去先交到report。Tommy叫我聽日同contractor開會，全程英文⋯救命
clips.text_en_b1: On site doing slope inspection today. Found a section where the factor of safety is only about 1.05 — basically right at the limit. Going to propose extra soil nails to bring the FoS up before the GI report goes out. Contractor meeting tomorrow, all in English.
clips.source_hint: Generic /biz/ thread repurposed for site-work English practice

signal.rationale: Civil engineering site context, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Spent most of the day on site carrying out a slope inspection, and one section came back with a factor of safety hovering around 1.05 — effectively sitting right on the edge of acceptable. I'll need to specify additional soil nails to bring that FoS up before the geotechnical interpretive report goes out. There's a contractor meeting scheduled for tomorrow, and apparently the whole thing will be conducted in English.
clips.text_en_c1: Spent the afternoon on site conducting a slope inspection, and the findings are, to put it mildly, uncomfortable. One particular section returned a factor of safety of roughly 1.05, which essentially means we are brushing against the regulatory threshold with virtually no margin to spare. Before the geotechnical interpretive report can be issued, I shall need to specify additional soil nails at carefully chosen spacings in order to elevate the FoS to an acceptable range. Tomorrow brings a contractor meeting, conducted entirely in English, where I will be required to defend the proposal to Tommy and the site team.
clips.text_en_c2: I spent the morning on a rather unforgiving slope inspection, and the numbers were, frankly, sobering: one particular stretch registered a factor of safety hovering around 1.05 — a value so marginal it might as well be engraved on a headstone. To salvage any semblance of compliance before the geotechnical interpretive report is tendered, I shall have to specify supplementary soil nailing, with all the attendant iterative recalculation that implies. Tommy has further compounded matters by scheduling a contractor meeting for tomorrow morning, conducted entirely in English, which is rather akin to asking a cat to swim. The irony of having to defend a 1.05 FoS to a roomful of sceptics, in a second language, at eight a.m., is not entirely lost on me.

clips.text_zh: 溫習緊RC load path，beam column joint搞到我頭都痛。FE chapter都未睇完，又要做structural calc。Sum Ho 何生下個禮拜要交份column schedule俾佢⋯🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Studying reinforced concrete load path tonight. Beam-column joints are killing me — shear transfer, confinement, anchorage, all of it. Need to finish the column schedule for Sum Ho by next week. FE manual is sitting on my desk judging me.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread repurposed for structural English practice

signal.rationale: Structural study context, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: I've been grinding through reinforced concrete load path revision tonight, and beam-column joints are absolutely wrecking me. Shear transfer, confinement detailing, anchorage requirements — every topic seems to pile up faster than I can process. On top of that, I still haven't finished the FE manual chapters, yet I need to deliver a complete column schedule to Sum Ho by next week. My desk has effectively become a guilt-ridden battlefield.
clips.text_en_c1: I have been revising reinforced concrete load paths until well past midnight, and the beam-column joint in particular is proving to be a formidable adversary. Shear transfer mechanisms, confinement detailing, development length, and anchorage requirements each demand a level of fluency that, frankly, I have not yet cultivated. Were that not enough, the FE manual chapters remain unfinished, lying accusingly on my desk, while a structural calc package waits in the queue. By next week, Sum Ho expects a complete column schedule, properly formatted and ready for review, and the deadline shows no sign of retreating.
clips.text_en_c2: I am presently engaged in what can only be described as an adversarial relationship with reinforced concrete load-path theory, and the beam-column joint in particular has become my principal antagonist. Shear transfer, confinement detailing, anchorage length — each clause of the code reads less like guidance than like an indictment of my own intellectual shortcomings. The FE manual sits accusingly upon my desk, its spine uncracked, while the column schedule for Sum Ho looms over the week like an impending tribunal. There is, I suspect, a particular irony in being undone not by calculation itself but by the bureaucratic apparatus that surrounds it — paperwork, it transpires, defeats the structural engineer more reliably than any axial load ever could.

clips.text_zh: 睇完條post真係心寒⋯AI model plateau咗，而家仲要fake story頂住VC。GPU泡沫爆咗之後會唔會連我份engineer工都冇埋？靠AI續命嘅日子越嚟越近 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: So they're admitting AI models have plateaued and they're coming up with some fake story about self restraint so they don't lose VC money. I'm so tired of this talmudic bullshit. And you thought you could get cheap GPUs after the AI bubble pops? Think again, they're all getting melted down.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread about GPUs being scrapped, not sold cheap

signal.rationale: Tech/AI commentary, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Apparently they're now openly admitting that AI models have plateaued, and instead of addressing it honestly, they're spinning some fabricated narrative about responsible scaling just to keep VC funding flowing. The whole thing feels deeply dishonest, frankly. And if you were hoping to pick up affordable GPUs once the AI bubble bursts, forget it — they're all being melted down. Even my engineering role could be on the chopping block soon.
clips.text_en_c1: Having read the post in its entirety, I find myself genuinely unsettled by what it implies for the broader technology landscape. The admission that frontier AI models have effectively plateaued, followed by the rather transparent attempt to repackage that stagnation as a principled exercise in self-restraint, is precisely the sort of narrative gymnastics one has come to expect from cash-hungry founders chasing the next venture round. The delusion that consumer-grade GPUs will become affordable once the bubble bursts is, frankly, laughable, since the units are being melted down for recovery rather than resold.
clips.text_en_c2: It is, upon reflection, a remarkably candid admission — frontier models have, by all credible accounts, plateaued, and rather than confront that reality with any rigour, the prevailing instinct appears to be the manufacture of a self-congratulatory narrative around restraint. The subtext, lest anyone miss it, is that venture capital must continue to flow uninterrupted, lest the entire edifice collapse under the weight of its own forward projections. As for those who imagine that a corrective revaluation might at least deliver affordable silicon: perish the thought — the GPUs, one suspects, will be ceremonially melted long before they reach a secondary market. I find myself weary of this particular species of financial sophistry, weary in a way that no quantity of caffeine can plausibly remedy.

clips.text_zh: Dario slowing down，Musk on board，Altman tapping out⋯frontier model真係慢落嚟？咁中國追過嚟嘅機會就大。我份工都係⋯算啦，睇住先。HK真係好細，5年後返Florida先算 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Dario slowing down, Musk on board, Altman tapping out. P(doom) status? 1%. The frontier models are slowing down. They are ready to deal with China. Total AI doomer victory on /pol/ tonight, anons are actually celebrating for once.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread claiming frontier AI slowdown and China angle

signal.rationale: Geopolitical AI commentary, no actionable trade

clips.text_en_b2: Dario is pumping the brakes, Musk has climbed on board, and Altman is quietly stepping back from the helm. With frontier development visibly decelerating, China's window to close the gap is widening significantly. The so-called doomers over on /pol/ are practically throwing a parade tonight, celebrating for once. My own position feels increasingly precarious, though I suppose I'll just watch how things unfold. Five years from now, Florida might be the move.
clips.text_en_c1: Dario appears to be throttling back, Musk has reportedly been brought into the fold, and Altman seems to be quietly disengaging, which collectively suggests that the frontier-model race is decelerating in ways that observers had previously dismissed as improbable. If the leading laboratories are genuinely willing to negotiate terms with Beijing rather than press ahead at full velocity, the geopolitical implications are considerable, and China's relative position strengthens accordingly. On /pol/ tonight, the prevailing mood borders on triumphant, with anons celebrating what they perceive as an unambiguous AI doomer victory.
clips.text_en_c2: The convergence is, at this juncture, difficult to dismiss as coincidence: Dario easing his pace, Musk recalibrating his rhetoric, Altman quietly withdrawing from public combat — the signal is unmistakable, even if each actor disavows any coordinated intent. P(doom), for those keeping score, sits at a rather restrained one percent, which is itself a kind of tell. The frontier, in other words, is decelerating, and the implications for the China file are as obvious as they are uncomfortable. /pol/ is, predictably, in a state of subdued euphoria — anons actually savouring a rare win rather than merely anticipating one. As for my own position in this matrix: I shall observe, with professional detachment, until such time as relocation to Florida becomes operationally tenable.

clips.text_zh: 睇完條post諗下自己⋯2025年83kg肥佬，cut到65kg skinnyfat，依家lean bulk返上80kg。bench 1 plate 3x8⋯同條post差唔多level 🤡 肥仔信仲叫我聽日一齊gym⋯lol
clips.text_en_b1: How do I know when I've bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat? In May 2025 I was 83kg fat, almost no muscle. Aggressive cut till mid April 2026, down to 65kg skinnyfat, couldn't bench even the 20kg bar. Then lean bulked back up to 80kg. Bench 3x8 at 1 plate, squat 3x6 at 90kg, deadlift 3x8 at 120kg.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking when to switch from bulk to cut

signal.rationale: Fitness progression question, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Reading that post hit a little too close to home, so I figured I'd map out my own journey. Back in May 2025, I tipped the scales at 83kg with virtually no muscle to speak of. I committed to an aggressive cut that dragged me down to a skinnyfat 65kg by mid-April 2026, barely handling the empty 20kg bar. Since then I've been lean bulking back up to 80kg, hitting bench 3x8 at one plate.
clips.text_en_c1: Reading the original post prompted a somewhat uncomfortable degree of self-recognition, since the trajectory described mirrors my own rather closely. In May 2025 I tipped the scales at a distinctly soft eighty-three kilograms, whereupon I committed to an aggressive cut that, by mid-April 2026, had reduced me to a decidedly skinnyfat sixty-five, at which point even an empty twenty-kilogram barbell felt punitive on the chest. A lean bulk thereafter restored me to roughly eighty kilograms, where I now bench three sets of eight at one plate, squat three sets of six at ninety kilograms, and deadlift three sets of eight at one hundred and twenty.
clips.text_en_c2: Having read that thread with more than passing interest, I find myself confronted by an unflattering mirror — the trajectory is, in essence, my own, rendered in a stranger's spreadsheet. May of 2025 found me at eighty-three kilograms, adipose and apologetic, possessing neither aesthetics nor athletic capacity to recommend the physique. I committed thereafter to an aggressive cut, enduring until April 2026, at which point I had arrived at sixty-five kilograms of rather pitiable skinnyfat — a state so aesthetically desolate that even the empty barbell defeated me. A subsequent lean bulk has restored me to roughly eighty kilograms, and the lifts have followed: bench three by eight at one plate, squat three by six at ninety, deadlift three by eight at one-twenty.
